title: Corporate Flight Bookings
statement: There are n flights numbered 1..n. Each booking [first, last, seats] reserves that many seats on every flight from first to last inclusive. Return a list where entry i is the total seats reserved on flight i+1.

large_tests.gen_code:
import random
def gen():
    r = random.Random(9)
    n = 100000
    b = []
    for _ in range(100000):
        f = r.randint(1, n)
        b.append([f, r.randint(f, n), r.randint(1, 100)])
    return [b, n]

hints.1_question: Adding seats to a whole range one flight at a time is slow. What if you only marked where the range starts and where it stops?
hints.2_nudge: Store changes instead of totals: +seats where the range begins, -seats just after it ends. Then a running sum rebuilds the totals.
hints.3_big_hint: diff size n+1. diff[first-1] += seats; diff[last] -= seats. Finally out[i] = out[i-1] + diff[i].

known_bugs.name: off by one: treats flights as 0-based
known_bugs.followup: Flights are numbered from 1 but list positions from 0. Which list position should flight 1 map to?

known_bugs.name: difference array too small (index error)
known_bugs.followup: What if a booking runs through the very last flight? Which index do you write the '-seats' marker at?

known_bugs.name: cancels the booking one flight early
known_bugs.followup: A booking [1, 2, 10] should cover flights 1 and 2. At which list index must the -10 marker go so flight 2 is still included?

followups: Why is a difference array the 'inverse' of a prefix sum?
How would you handle many range updates interleaved with point queries?
